# t22.1 — Default Agent Discovery and Canonical Skill Catalog

## Result

`C-004` and `C-005` are remediated without moving policy into the presentation layer:

- `LoadAgentUseCase` now normalizes absent CLI add-ons to an empty immutable list and always
  delegates to `LoadAgentDefinitionsPort`; the adapter remains responsible for merging configured
  defaults such as `./agents` and `./.github/agents`.
- `AgentConfigLoader` returns the valid global skills from the same discovery pass used to enrich
  agents.
- `AgentDefinitionLoaderAdapter` publishes that complete snapshot through the new
  `ManageSkillCatalogPort`.
- `SkillRegistry` is the singleton infrastructure adapter for that port and atomically replaces an
  immutable ordered snapshot, preventing stale skills and partial refreshes.
- `ExecuteSkillUseCase` lists and resolves skills only through the canonical outbound port;
  `ApplicationPortFactory` no longer injects concrete registry method references.

## Layer Responsibility Evidence

| Layer | Responsibility retained |
|---|---|
| Presentation | Supplies only optional CLI directory add-ons |
| Application | Orchestrates agent loading and skill execution through ports |
| Application ports | Defines agent loading and canonical discovered-skill catalog contracts |
| Infrastructure | Merges configured paths, parses files, and owns the catalog adapter |
| Domain | Keeps agent and skill values free of framework dependencies |

The full architecture suite includes 22/22 passing `LayerDependencyRulesTest` cases, including
application-to-adapter isolation, infrastructure-to-port direction, cycle checks, and complete
compiled-class coverage.

## Discriminating Packaged-CLI Coverage

`PackagedCliSmokeIT` now uses isolated temporary working directories and exact known fixtures:

1. `discoversAgentsFromConfiguredDefaultDirectory` runs the shaded JAR with `list` and **no**
   `--agents-dir`, then requires `packaged-default-agent` and rejects `No agents found.` This fails
   if the application use case restores its empty-input short circuit.
2. `listsDiscoveredSkillsFromCanonicalExecutionCatalog` supplies an explicit agent directory to
   bypass the first defect, runs `skill --list`, requires `packaged-catalog-skill`, and rejects
   `No skills found.` This fails when discovery and execution use separate catalogs.

The former assertion that accepted either an empty or populated inventory was removed.
